cases.name: Bonnie Gayle Ryther
cases.narrative:
A week after she disappeared, her battered body was found in some woods about 30 feet from where her Ford Pinto had been abandoned.

In his confession, he said they met in Wayside Park and were smoking dope and he got angry and killed her in her car. He said he partially buried her body and left it and her car in a park but couldn’t remember exactly which one. He also made a point during the confession to mention he liked to drink Busch Tallboy beers. Incidentally, Bonnie’s Ford Pinto had been found abandoned in Ferry Park, Fort Walton Beach. Her battered body would be found 6 days later, partially buried, with a few cans of Busch Tallboy beers scattered around her remains.

cases.name: Ronda Taylor
cases.narrative:
She was found stabbed to death and her body was left in the backseat of her car in Fort Walton Beach, FL.

(She) was found at about noon by a man who was walking down Tupelo Avenue in Fort Walton Beach. Reports say the man, Ronald Browning, passed by a silver Buick and glanced in the window.

“I thought it was a blow-up, a balloon doll,” Browning recalled. “For some reason, I went back to check. I couldn’t believe it."

Taylor’s nude body was found “crumpled” in the backseat of her car, according to investigators’ statements at the time. Her head was against the rear seat, just below window level. Her throat had been cut and she had stab wounds on her hands and arms. There were also scratches on her legs. The body had apparently been moved from the location where the murder took place.

Mark said that he and Ronda were looking for some crack cocaine to purchase. He said that the person who sold it to them, an African American male, he stated, ended up coming with them. They had exited her car and after doing the drugs, Ronda got extremely hot and removed her clothing. Her and Mark Riebe proceeded to get into a heated argument where he stabbed her repeatedly. The African American male tried to step in and Riebe stabbed him in the hand as well. Afterwards, Mark put Ronda’s body back in the backseat of her silver Buick and parked it where his wife at the time was working that night. Ronda was found undressed and her clothing found in the car with no blood on it and no cuts from the stab wounds, backing up Riebe’s story. Also, noteworthy, years later the only DNA found in the car belonged to a bloody towel and it was eventually tested and did belong to an African American male that police were not even aware of was at the scene, not until Mark Riebe’s confession that is.
